@copilot Update this PR directly with a behavior-preserving separation of per-registry registration ownership from shared metric recording.

Keep DropwizardMetricsAdapter as the per-registry MetricRegistryListener, owning the OpenTelemetry meter, registration maps, and gauge callback lifecycle. Move the four static VirtualFields and the counterAdd, histogramUpdate, meterMark, and timerUpdate recording helpers into a small DropwizardMetricsRecorder utility with static methods and no singleton instance. Give the adapter narrowly scoped access to bind/unbind metric-object-to-instrument associations through the recorder; keep registration ownership out of the recorder and avoid unnecessary abstractions.

Update CounterInstrumentation, HistogramInstrumentation, MeterInstrumentation, and TimerInstrumentation to call the recorder directly, and remove DropwizardSingletons once unused. Relevant production sources are under instrumentation/dropwizard/dropwizard-metrics-4.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/dropwizardmetrics/v4_0/.

Preserve this PR's per-registry isolation fix and all existing gauge, counter, histogram, meter, and timer behavior, including name handling, removal semantics, and nanosecond-to-millisecond conversion. Recording must continue to find the instrument attached by the owning registry's adapter, and removing a different same-named metric object from another registry must not detach the remaining object's association. This is a responsibility cleanup, not a change to metric semantics or a broader instrumentation redesign.

Retain the existing regression tests, verify the recording paths and per-registry isolation, and add only focused tests needed for this refactor. Run the narrowest applicable formatting and existing test tasks.

Target the existing PR head in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation on copilot/create-dropwizard-per-registry-ownership, rather than requesting a new PR. Keep the branch assigned by GitHub Copilot cloud agent; do not rename it or create a replacement branch. Keep any platform-assigned follow-up branch if GitHub creates one.

replies.body: Implemented in 544c2e9d. The adapter now owns per-registry registration and gauge lifecycle; `DropwizardMetricsRecorder` owns the virtual fields and static recording methods, the advices call it directly, and `DropwizardSingletons` is removed. Added a focused same-name counter removal regression. The module tests and `spotlessJavaCheck` pass.

@copilot Update this existing PR #21370 directly on `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation:copilot/create-dropwizard-per-registry-ownership`. Keep the branch assigned by GitHub Copilot cloud agent and any platform-assigned follow-up branch. Do not rename or replace branches or request a new PR. Preserve this draft PR's existing base `copilot/prefactoring-dropwizard-metric-recording` from #21379. Do not modify the lower PR or other branches.

Fix the Java agent Dropwizard gauge retention when an app is undeployed and its `MetricRegistry` becomes unreachable without calling `remove()`. `MetricRegistryInstrumentation` in this PR gives each registry its own `DropwizardMetricsAdapter`, but `DropwizardMetricsAdapter.onGaugeAdded` still registers a lambda capturing the app's `Gauge` directly with the long-lived agent SDK. The SDK can pin both the callback's defining loader and the gauge's app loader even after the registry is gone. This is independent of the saved TCCL edge addressed by open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java#9045. Do not change the SDK, versions, TCCL behavior, or agent API bridge. Work independently of the Micrometer fix.

Keep the real callback strongly owned by the source registry's lifetime, for example in its per-registry listener, while the gauge should report. Pass a bootstrap-loaded weak delegate to the SDK, using the existing `javaagent-bootstrap` `WeakRefConsumer` where appropriate, and have it close the SDK registration when the real callback is collected. Trace the entire SDK-held graph including the close action; do not give it a strong path back to a Gauge, app-defined callback class, adapter, or registry. Do not anchor the registration to the gauge alone if that would keep a dead registry's registration alive when the gauge is separately referenced. Keep any lifecycle state per registry and preserve explicit removal and the existing same-name isolation in either removal order. Keep the recorder refactor, synchronous metric behavior, name handling, and emitted telemetry unchanged. Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the applicable `.github/instructions` files, especially `instrumentation-state.instructions.md`, before introducing weak ownership.

Add a focused agent-path regression demonstrating that the gauge reports while its owning registry is alive and that an otherwise unreachable disposable app loader can be collected without explicit gauge removal, with the stale SDK registration removed on collection. Use a neutral registration thread context loader in that test if necessary to isolate the callback edge from the current SDK's separate TCCL hold. Keep the existing per-registry regressions. Run the narrowest applicable `spotlessApply` directly, then the focused Dropwizard tests using the repository's required JDK if available. Report actual results or blockers.

replies.body: Implemented in 743830f2. The adapter now strongly owns each live gauge callback, while the SDK receives a bootstrap `WeakRefConsumer` that closes its registration after callback collection; explicit removal and per-registry isolation remain intact. Added the disposable-loader agent regression. Module `spotlessApply` passed and all 9 Dropwizard agent tests passed on Java 25. CI triage could not download logs because `gh` lacks `GH_TOKEN`; CodeQL was attempted but timed out, and its tool instructed not to retry.

threads.body: [Javaagent] The callback and handle are published separately, so a concurrent registry removal can run after `otelGauges.put(...)` but before this line. `onGaugeRemoved()` then finds no callback and removes/closes the handle, after which this put leaves an orphan callback strongly retaining the removed Dropwizard gauge (and any application state it captures) for the remaining registry lifetime. Please publish the callback and handle together as one registration entry and remove that entry atomically, closing its handle outside the state update.

replies.body: Fixed in `59e92202`. The callback and SDK handle now share one entry per gauge in the registry's listener. Removal takes out that entry in one operation and then closes the handle.

@copilot Fix the gauge removal race in this existing draft PR #21370 on `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation:copilot/create-dropwizard-per-registry-ownership`. Update this PR directly. Keep the GitHub Copilot cloud agent's assigned branch and any platform-assigned follow-up branch. Do not rename or replace branches or request a new PR. Keep the existing base `copilot/prefactoring-dropwizard-metric-recording` from #21379 and leave the lower PR unchanged.

In `DropwizardMetricsAdapter` at `743830f2`, `onGaugeAdded` puts the SDK handle in `otelGauges` before saving the callback in `gaugeCallbacks`. Dropwizard 4.0 can notify `onGaugeRemoved` between the two puts. Removal closes the handle, then the add leaves a callback that holds the removed app gauge for the listener's lifetime. This is the issue in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/21370#discussion_r4639545312.

Use a single per-registry map entry per gauge name to own the strong callback and its SDK handle. Publish and remove them as a pair, and close the removed handle outside the map update or any instrumentation lock. Keep the bootstrap `WeakRefConsumer` and its close-on-collection behavior. Preserve same-name isolation across registries, explicit removal, and the existing recording behavior. Limit the concurrency change to the new split-publication window; leave SDK code, TCCL behavior, Micrometer, and the recorder refactor alone.

Keep the disposable-loader, both gauge removal order, and counter regressions. Keep the source registry reachable through the positive gauge assertion in `gaugeDoesNotRetainApplicationClassLoader`, then drop it without calling `remove()`. If you can test the removal window deterministically with existing test tools, add that coverage without sleeps or production test hooks. Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the applicable `.github/instructions` files. Run the module's `spotlessApply` directly, then the focused Dropwizard 4.0 agent tests on JDK 25, and report actual results or blockers.

replies.body: Fixed in 59e92202. Gauge callbacks and their SDK handles are now published and removed together in a single per-name registration entry; replaced and removed handles are closed after the map update.
